column1: # The operand positions of loft's syntax — the slot register of the slot matrix (@PLN221).
# Columns, tab-separated: id, family, rule, count, runs, type, statement[, declaration].
#   rule    the formal rule that states how often this operand runs (`E-Left`, cited without
#           its `@FR-` sigil); `-` when no rule states it yet, which `check` lists as owed.
#   count   once | first | cond | step — exactly once; exactly once AND before the statement
#           reads anything else, so that binding the operand first is what the rules say
#           even when the operand writes what the statement works on; zero or one, decided
#           by another operand; once per iteration.
#   runs    how often the operand runs in THIS statement, in the prelude's world.
#   type    what the slot takes; a filler of that type goes in (scripts/syntax_fillers.tsv).
#           `type@kind,kind` keeps the slot to the collection kinds it has a meaning in
#           (a keyed collection has no rendering; `#index` is not for an `index`), and
#           `type!filler,filler` keeps out fillers that are not of the type the statement
#           needs (a nullable integer into a narrow field).  What the compiler still
#           refuses after that is a refusal of the LANGUAGE, and is listed as one.
#   statement  one statement of `main` in scripts/syntax_slots_prelude.loft; `<S>` is the slot.
#           Where a `{` follows the slot, the slot stands in parentheses: a block as the
#           operand would otherwise be read as the statement's own body (`for n in 0..{…}
#           {…}` is an open-ended range over the first block, and never ends).
#   declaration  an optional top-level declaration the statement needs; `<S>` may sit there
#           instead.  A function declared there takes `<ENV>` as its parameters and is
#           called with `<ARGS>`: every value of the prelude's world, so that a filler finds
#           the names it uses there as it does in `main`.  `<ENV -tk>` leaves a name
#           out and `<ENV: c h i>` keeps only the named ones (the same after `ARGS`), for a
#           declaration that cannot take the whole world: a generator with the world's
#           collection of records or its tuple among its parameters ends the interpreter,
#           which is a defect of its own, so that slot names the values its fillers use.
#           `<BIND>` in it marks where the bound-first twin binds the operand (`t0 = …;`),
#           which gives a slot inside a declaration its twin; without it the plain variable
#           is what the cell is compared with.
# A new operator, keyword or `#` attribute adds a row here, or a line in
# scripts/syntax_outside.tsv saying why it takes no operand: `slot_matrix.py check` fails
# until one of the two exists.
